startup_idea: A WhatsApp bot that reminds dental clinic patients about appointments and collects deposits
mission: Automate WhatsApp reminders and deposit collection for solo dental clinics in tier‑2 India so they never lose revenue to missed appointments.
problem: Clinic staff spend hours chasing no‑show patients because appointments are forgotten, leading to lost revenue and scheduling chaos at the exact moment a reminder is needed.
target_customer: Solo dental clinic owners in tier‑2 Indian cities (₹10‑20 L annual turnover) who manually track appointments and need a cheap, automated way to reduce no‑shows.

business_model.name: Free
features: Up to 10 WhatsApp reminders per month

financial_snapshot.burn_breakdown: Cloudflare Registrar (annual domain spread monthly): ₹68; Freelance UI tweaks (5 hrs @ ₹500/hr): ₹2,500; Marketing budget (targeted Facebook/WhatsApp ads): ₹10,000

go_to_market: WhatsApp Community Outreach: Join 5 local dental WhatsApp groups and send 20 personalized voice-note messages/day to clinic owners
Facebook Lead Ads: Run FB lead ad campaign targeting tier‑2 dental clinic owners, spend ₹6,000/month, 150 leads
Compile a list of 200 solo dental clinics in tier‑2 cities via local business directories and WhatsApp groups.
Send a personalized 3‑sentence DM referencing their clinic’s no‑show pain point.
Offer a 2‑week free trial of 10 WhatsApp reminders with deposit link.
Schedule a 15‑minute demo call to walk through the reminder flow and ROI.
Close the deal with a limited‑time ₹399/month sign‑up and onboard via shared Google Sheet.
product_mvp: WhatsApp reminder scheduling and automatic message sending
Razorpay deposit payment link embedded in reminder message
Clinic dashboard to view appointments and reminder status
Initialize a new Next.js app with TypeScript using npx create-next-app@latest dental-whatsapp-bot --ts --app
Install TailwindCSS and shadcn/ui: npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer && npx tailwindcss init -p && npx shadcn-ui@latest init
Create a free Supabase project, note the URL and anon key, and add @supabase/supabase-js to the project
Add Supabase client initialization in lib/supabase.ts and enable Supabase Auth for clinic staff login
Register a .com domain via Cloudflare Registrar (≈₹820/year) and configure DNS to point to Vercel
Connect the GitHub repo to Vercel and deploy the app using the free Hobby plan
Set up Meta WhatsApp Cloud API: create a Meta developer app, obtain a phone‑number ID and permanent access token, store them in Supabase env variables

Implement an API route (/api/schedule) that stores appointment data in Supabase, queues a WhatsApp message via fetch to https://graph.facebook.com/v16.0/{PHONE_ID}/messages, and logs message count; add a Supabase Edge Function that runs daily to check WhatsApp usage via the API and sends a Resend email alert when usage exceeds 80% of the 500‑message quota
Integrate Razorpay Checkout: generate a payment link in the reminder message using Razorpay’s API and include it in the WhatsApp payload
Populate the dashboard page, test the full flow with a dummy clinic account, fix bugs, and push the final version to production

revenue_targets.notes: 10 paying customers. Early adopters acquired via founder outreach and low‑budget ads
25 paying customers. Growth through referrals and continued ad spend
40 paying customers. Stabilized acquisition, churn minimal

competition.name: Practo for Clinics
competition.differentiator: We charge ₹1,250/month versus their ₹3,500 and deliver WhatsApp messages instead of costly SMS, fitting the low‑budget market.

competition.name: Karix (formerly mTalkz)
competition.differentiator: Our product is pre‑configured for dental appointment flows, while Karix is a generic API requiring developer time and higher fees.

competition.name: ClinicMitra
competition.differentiator: ClinicMitra offers only SMS reminders; we win by using WhatsApp with rich media and deposit links.

key_conflicts.title: Economics: The pricing of ₹399/month violates the hard rule 'Bootstrapped pricing must never exceed $5/month' (approx ₹415, but ₹39
key_conflicts.description: The pricing of ₹399/month violates the hard rule 'Bootstrapped pricing must never exceed $5/month' (approx ₹415, but ₹399 is dangerously close and often considered above the psychological threshold for 'low-cost' in this context, more importantly, the revenue target of 35 customers in 30 days is unrealistic for a cold-start B2B SaaS in Tier-2 India with only ₹10k marketing budget and manual outreach, leading to a cash flow gap if churn is higher than assumed or sales are slower. Fix: Lower the Pro plan price to ₹299/month to stay safely under the $5 equivalent and improve conversion odds in price-sensitive Tier-2 markets. Adjust revenue targets to be more conservative (e.g., 10 customers by Day 30, 25 by Day 60) to align with realistic cold-start B2B sales cycles in India, ensuring the burn rate (₹12.5k) is covered by the lower but more attainable MRR sooner.

key_conflicts.title: Builder: The plan assumes the Meta WhatsApp Cloud API free tier (1,000 messages) covers usage, but for a clinic sending reminders
key_conflicts.description: The plan assumes the Meta WhatsApp Cloud API free tier (1,000 messages) covers usage, but for a clinic sending reminders to multiple patients, 1,000 messages is very low (approx 33 patients/month if 1 reminder each). Most clinics will exceed this, incurring per-message costs that are not accounted for in the 'Free' tool cost or the unit economics, potentially eroding the ₹399 margin or making the service unprofitable for high-volume clinics. Fix: Update the tool costs to include an estimated buffer for WhatsApp message overages (e.g., ₹500/month) or clarify that the Free tier is a trial limit and the Pro plan includes a specific message quota (e.g., 500 messages) with overage charges passed to the customer. Adjust the MVP steps to include a check for message limits and a fallback or notification when the limit is near.

key_conflicts.title: Growth: The channel 'LinkedIn Outreach' with a target of 25 new customers/month at ₹0 CAC is highly unrealistic for solo dental
key_conflicts.description: The channel 'LinkedIn Outreach' with a target of 25 new customers/month at ₹0 CAC is highly unrealistic for solo dental clinic owners in Tier-2 India. These owners are rarely active on LinkedIn for business development; they are more likely on WhatsApp, local Facebook groups, or referred by peers. Relying on this channel will lead to wasted time and missed revenue targets. Fix: Replace 'LinkedIn Outreach' with 'WhatsApp Community Groups & Local Dental Associations' or 'Direct WhatsApp Outreach to Clinic Owners' (sourced from local directories). Adjust the tactic to involve joining local business/dental WhatsApp groups and sending personalized voice notes or messages, which is more culturally appropriate and effective for Tier-2 India. Recalculate CAC and customer acquisition numbers based on this more realistic channel.

key_conflicts.title: Growth: Facebook Lead Ads: CAC ₹60 but spend / customers = ₹600.
key_conflicts.description: Facebook Lead Ads: CAC ₹60 but spend / customers = ₹600. Fix: Set cac to 600.

key_conflicts.title: Economics: The Pro plan price of ₹299/month is below the variable cost of serving a customer. The WhatsApp Cloud API charges per co
key_conflicts.description: The Pro plan price of ₹299/month is below the variable cost of serving a customer. The WhatsApp Cloud API charges per conversation (approx ₹15-₹20 per 24h session in India). A single active patient requiring reminders and deposit collection will consume at least one conversation, costing the founder more than the revenue generated. This creates a negative unit economics trap where every new customer increases the burn rate rather than reducing it. Fix: Increase the Pro plan price to at least ₹999/month to ensure a positive gross margin after API costs. Alternatively, introduce a per-message fee structure or limit the number of active conversations included in the subscription to align costs with revenue. Update the MRR targets and break-even calculations accordingly.

key_conflicts.title: Builder: The build plan omits the Meta Business Verification process, which is mandatory for the WhatsApp Cloud API to send templ
key_conflicts.description: The build plan omits the Meta Business Verification process, which is mandatory for the WhatsApp Cloud API to send template messages (like appointment reminders) at scale. This process typically takes 3-7 days and requires legal business documents. Without this, the MVP cannot legally send automated reminders to users who have not previously messaged the business, rendering the core product non-functional for the intended use case. Fix: Add a step to initiate Meta Business Verification immediately upon starting the build. Include a contingency plan for the verification delay (e.g., using a 'Click-to-Chat' flow for initial opt-in if verification is pending) or extend the timeline to 4-6 weeks to account for this administrative bottleneck.

key_conflicts.title: Growth: The CAC calculation for Facebook Lead Ads is unrealistic. A CAC of ₹60 implies a 100% conversion rate from lead to payin
key_conflicts.description: The CAC calculation for Facebook Lead Ads is unrealistic. A CAC of ₹60 implies a 100% conversion rate from lead to paying customer (₹6,000 spend / 100 leads = ₹60/lead, but only 10 customers = ₹600 actual CAC). In B2B SaaS, lead-to-close rates are typically 5-10%, not 100%. The plan assumes that every lead generated will convert, which is not possible without a sales team or highly qualified intent. Fix: Recalculate CAC based on a realistic conversion rate (e.g., 10% of leads become customers). This will raise the CAC to approximately ₹600. Adjust the marketing budget to reflect that ₹6,000 will only yield 1-2 customers, not 10. Increase the budget or shift focus to higher-conversion channels like direct founder outreach to reduce reliance on paid ads for early traction.

final_verdict: The plan is fundamentally misaligned with the bootstrapped constraint and Indian market reality. The revenue model relies on a pricing tier (₹299) that fails to cover the variable costs of the WhatsApp Cloud API, leading to a negative gross margin per customer. Furthermore, the growth strategy underestimates the difficulty of acquiring B2B customers in tier-2 cities via cold DMs and Facebook ads, while the build plan ignores the significant friction of Meta Business Verification, which can delay launch beyond the 2-4 week window.
